title: DHCP Systems Engineering: Core Infrastructure
subject: DHCP
description: Master the logic of dynamic addressing. From broadcast boundaries and relay agents to Active Directory authorization and failover replication, these 10 scenarios cover the essential lifecycle of an IP lease in an enterprise environment.
reportOverview: This report analyzes your diagnostic accuracy regarding DHCP infrastructure. Use it to verify your understanding of the DORA process, cross-subnet communication, and high-availability synchronization.
evidenceInstructions:
Instructions:
1) Analyze the symptom and examine the provided technical evidence.
2) Choose the initial investigative step to gather more data.
3) Identify the root cause based on network logic.
4) Select the best fix and review the Resolution Insight to master the concept.

tickets.title: New Server Authorization Block
tickets.summary: A secondary DHCP server (DC-02) is installed. The service starts, but the console shows a red down arrow and clients are not getting IPs.
artifact: Event Viewer: System Log, Event ID 1046
Message: The DHCP service has determined that it is not authorized to service clients.

triage.q: What should you check in the DHCP console to verify the server's operational status in the domain?
options: Check for the 'Authorized' status in the server node properties
Check if the server is in the 'Schema Admins' group
Check if the server can ping 8.8.8.8

diagnosis.q: Why is the server refusing to issue leases?
options: It is a 'Rogue' server because it hasn't been authorized in Active Directory
The client is on a different VLAN
Right-click the server in the DHCP console and select 'Authorize'

debrief.summary: Authorization is a security guardrail in Active Directory.
debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: Active Directory maintains a list of 'Authorized' DHCP servers in the Configuration partition. This prevents unauthorized servers from joining the network and handing out 'poisoned' gateway or DNS information to clients.

tickets.title: The Relay Agent Requirement
tickets.summary: Users in VLAN 20 cannot get IPs, but users in VLAN 10 (where the server is) have no issues.
artifact: DHCP Server: Only has a physical NIC in VLAN 10.

triage.q: Since DHCP Discover is a broadcast, how does it cross a router?
options: It can't, unless a Relay Agent/IP Helper is configured
It uses DNS to find the server
Router is dropping the DHCP broadcast

fix.q: How do you bridge the connection?
options: Configure 'IP Helper-Address' on the VLAN 20 gateway

debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: DHCP relies on the 'DORA' broadcast. Routers block these by default. A Relay Agent (or IP Helper) intercepts the broadcast, wraps it in a unicast packet, and forwards it directly to the DHCP server's IP.

tickets.title: Addressing the 'BAD_ADDRESS' Entries
tickets.summary: The DHCP scope is filling up with 'BAD_ADDRESS' entries, and users report IP conflicts.
artifact: DHCP Console: Many leases listed as 'BAD_ADDRESS'
Context: Static IPs were assigned to printers without creating reservations.

triage.q: What does 'BAD_ADDRESS' specifically indicate in a Windows DHCP scope?
options: The server pinged the IP before offering it and received a response, indicating a conflict
A device has a static IP that overlaps with the dynamic range
The lease time is too long
Create an Exclusion Range for the static IPs

debrief.summary: Conflict detection saves the network from duplicate IPs.
debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: When 'Conflict Detection' is enabled, the server sends an ICMP Echo Request before an 'Offer'. If a device responds, the server marks the IP as 'BAD' to protect the network, but the real fix is excluding those IPs from the pool entirely.

tickets.title: Scope Exhaustion Crisis
tickets.summary: New devices in the office cannot connect. The DHCP console shows 100% utilization for the subnet.

triage.q: What is the most immediate way to see if there are IPs that can be reclaimed?
options: Check the number of active leases vs. the pool size

diagnosis.q: Why did the scope run out of IPs?
options: The range is too small for the number of devices and the lease duration is too long to recycle IPs

fix.q: What is the best long-term fix?
options: Expand the range or shorten the lease duration

debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: High-turnover environments (like guest Wi-Fi) require short lease times (hours). Professional environments with many devices require larger pools (/23 or /22) to prevent exhaustion.

tickets.title: Failover Out of Sync
tickets.summary: Two servers are in a failover relationship, but the 'Partner Down' state persists after a reboot.

triage.q: Which port must be open on the firewall for two DHCP servers to replicate their databases?

diagnosis.q: What is causing the sync failure?
options: The servers can't talk to each other over the failover port

fix.q: How do you restore the relationship?
options: Ensure port 647 is open and force a manual replication
Delete the scope on Server B

debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: DHCP Failover uses TCP Port 647 for the 'Failover Protocol.' If this port is blocked, the servers cannot sync their lease databases, leading to potential IP conflicts if both servers try to issue the same IP.

tickets.title: Missing Option 003: No Gateway
tickets.summary: Users get an IP address and can ping other local PCs, but they cannot access the Internet.

triage.q: Which DHCP Option provides the 'Default Gateway' to the client?

options: The client has no gateway and doesn't know how to send traffic outside its subnet

fix.q: How do you fix this for all users?
options: Configure Scope Option 003 with the correct Router IP
Manually type the gateway on every PC

debrief.summary: DHCP provides more than just an IP.
debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: An IP and Mask allow Layer 2 (local) communication. Without Option 003 (Router), the client has no routing table entry for '0.0.0.0', making it impossible to reach any address outside its own local broadcast domain.

tickets.title: DNS Dynamic Update Failure
tickets.summary: DHCP is working, but the DNS server is not being updated with the new hostnames of the clients.

triage.q: Where does the DHCP server manage its interaction with the DNS server?
options: The DNS tab in DHCP Server or Scope properties
DHCP is not instructed to tell DNS about new leases
Enable 'Dynamically update DNS records only if requested by DHCP clients' (or always)

debrief.summary: DHCP and DNS must work as a team.
debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: In a Windows environment, the DHCP server can act as a proxy for the client, updating the DNS 'A' and 'PTR' records as soon as a lease is issued. This ensures the name resolution stays accurate even as IPs change.

tickets.title: Reservation Conflict
tickets.summary: A CEO's laptop is supposed to always get 192.168.1.50, but it keeps getting a random IP from the pool.

triage.q: What unique identifier does DHCP use to match a reservation to a specific device?

options: The MAC address in the reservation doesn't match the actual hardware
Update the reservation with the correct MAC address
Delete the reservation and use static

debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: A DHCP Reservation is an 'infinite lease' for a specific MAC address. If the MAC address is even one character off, the server won't recognize the 'Discover' packet as belonging to that reservation and will pull a random IP from the general pool.

tickets.title: MCLT and the Temporary Lease
tickets.summary: During a failover test, clients are getting leases that only last for 1 hour, even though the scope is set for 8 days.
artifact: Current Status: Primary server is offline.

triage.q: What does MCLT stand for in DHCP Failover settings?

diagnosis.q: Why is the lease so short (1 hour)?
options: The partner server can only issue leases for the duration of the MCLT when the primary is down
The server is running out of memory

fix.q: Is this a bug or intended behavior?
options: It is intended; wait for the primary to return or adjust MCLT if longer outages are expected
It is a bug; reinstall DHCP

debrief.summary: MCLT is a safety buffer for failover.
debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: The Maximum Client Lead Time (MCLT) is the maximum time a partner server can extend a lease for a client beyond the time known by the primary server. This prevents 'duplicate leases' if the servers lose communication but both remain running.

tickets.title: Multicast Scope Confusion
tickets.summary: A video conferencing app isn't working correctly. The vendor says you need a MADCAP scope.
artifact: Current Setup: Only IPv4 Unicast Scopes (10.0.0.x)
Requirement: Class D IP addresses (224.0.0.0 range).

triage.q: What type of scope is used to assign Multicast (Class D) addresses?

diagnosis.q: Why can't a standard scope handle this?
options: Standard scopes only handle one-to-one communication; Multicast is one-to-many
The IP range is too small

fix.q: What is the step to resolve?
options: Create a New Multicast Scope in the DHCP console

debrief.summary: Multicast requires a separate allocation logic.
debrief.takeaway: Resolution Insight: While standard DHCP handles Unicast (point-to-point) IPs, MADCAP (Multicast Address Dynamic Client Allocation Protocol) is used specifically to manage the assignment of temporary Multicast addresses for streaming and collaboration apps.
